Arch Support That Starts at the Source

Think of your foot’s arch like the Gateway Arch in Missouri—an engineering marvel held together by perfect balance and physics. Now imagine shifting one side of that arch just five feet to the left. What happens? It crumbles. Missouri’s skyline?

Flat...

Your foot works the same way. That elegant curve is supported by a key muscle and bone structure that stretches from the tip of your big toe, to your ankle. When narrow shoes squeeze your toes inward, it starts pushing that support away from its proper placement, which then weakens over time. And over years or decades, it can cause your arch to fall and other common foot conditions.

Frequently Asked Questions

settings.heading: What will wearing Correct Toes do?

settings.text:
With Correct Toes, you can:

  • Relieve foot pain while being active
  • Align toes back to their natural, anatomical position
  • Improve strength and flexibility of the toes and feet
  • Increase circulation to the ends of the toes
  • Enhance balance and stability

Correct Toes help splay the toes in the way that nature intended.

Why is this important?

We spend a lifetime in footwear that is too narrow at the ends of the toes. As a result, the shod adult foot shape differs from the unshod adult foot shape (and from the foot shape of infants, who are born with perfect feet).

Correct Toes work in a similar way to how braces work for teeth. Correct Toes place the toes into optimal alignment and slowly and progressively change the architecture of the foot.

The muscles of the foot adapt and strengthen accordingly. Toe alignment and foot strength has numerous positive effects on biomechanics, gait and injury prevention.

settings.heading: How long until I see results?

settings.text:
The time it takes for toe spacers to work varies depending on individual circumstances.

Most people may experience relief from foot discomfort almost immediately, while others may require a few days up to several weeks of consistent wear to notice an improvement.

When a foot has been deformed by decades in conventional shaped shoes, it takes time and maintanence to begin to undo the damage or lessen its effects.
